_comment: A routed squadron at the edge of its pursuer's reach keeps one couple() anchor instead of switching it every tick or two (#1801). A brittle player squadron (16 Cavalry at morale 0.5) stands on open ground; an enemy Infantry block (40 men, 10 files) 210 wu to its east, facing it, charges it with no player input. Measured 2026-11-06 on 7e3e49cd against main a37af5c0, seed 0: the squadron turns to meet it and fights from tick 226, routs at tick 325 still in contact (326 on main), and flees north with the infantry following at the edge of melee range. Its physical contact flag flips 4 times over ticks 420 to 455 (none on main), and its anchor's speed changes by 0.013 wu a tick on average over ticks 420 to 470 (0.009 on main). Its men's centroid has moved 64.5 wu 150 ticks after the rout and 337.2 wu after 300 (63.3 and 323.7 on main). It is still fleeing north when the clip ends at tick 560 and rallies at tick 686 (687 on main). When the #1801 fix was made the anchor flipped with the contact flag, changing speed by 0.55 wu a tick on average over ticks 420 to 470 on main a58c122e against 0.08 on the fix 45a9bb85, and the position checks at ticks 430 to 448 pinned where the fix's anchor stood then (9.5, 9.5, 10.2 and 7.5 wu from main a58c122e's). Re-pinned for #1915 with Ezra's approval of 2026-11-06 (https://github.com/Lacaedemon/sparta/issues/1915#issuecomment-6699756871), where a troop whose combat wheel falls more than 75 degrees behind an enemy among its ranks keeps wheeling instead of turning in place. The infantry's centre stands 24.5 to 29.6 wu from the squadron's anchor, inside its own footprint, so the bearing to it runs away faster than the wheel can turn: the heading trails the bearing to contact_point(enemy), the point the wheel turns toward, by 34.2 to 138.2 degrees over ticks 276 to 326 (traced in _wheel_combat_reface before each tick's turn) and first trails it by more than 75 degrees at tick 287 (76.2). On main the squadron turned in place there; its contact flag dropped at tick 302 (301 or 302 on seeds 1 to 4), one morale step was missed, and it routed at tick 326 (302 on seed 2). Now it loses contact only at tick 228, just after first meeting the infantry, its morale reaches 0 at tick 324, and it routs at tick 325 still in contact on seeds 0 to 4. So the setup checks read ROUTING at 325 and 326 and in contact at 326. The four anchor-position checks at ticks 430 to 448 were re-pinned for #1913 with Ezra's approval of 2026-11-07 (wave 17 project thread). Measured 2026-11-07 on 17f3671f, seed 0: the router now stands at (561.09, 955.4), (561.75, 951.35), (562.35, 946.96) and (562.91, 942.22) at those ticks, where the earlier pins stood 18.9 to 20.7 wu to the east and north of that. They moved because the router's whole flight moved after the #1806 combat-wheel change, which the 2026-11-06 figures above predate, so even forcing the earlier anchor left them 17 to 22 wu off; #1936 fixed the anchor flicker the pins protected, and #1825 and #1934 have since merged. Seeds 1 to 4 read within 1.5 wu of seed 0 on each component (largest 1.45 wu, y at tick 448), inside the tol of 3.0 wu kept from the earlier pins. On 17f3671f the router's anchor leaves its front ranks once on every seed 0 to 4, at about tick 454 to 460 (a few ticks after the checks), and not at all over ticks 415 to 450.

shape_residual.reason: The infantry pursuer (uid 1) deforms while it follows the router at the edge of melee range, from about tick 440 to the clip's end, and the deformation is pre-existing (36.0 on main 45a9bb85 on the first sample set). Measured 2026-11-10 on aef5b476, seeds 0 to 4, every exemption removed. On dense 2-tick FULL dumps over ticks 2 to 600 the verdict FAILS on every seed: worst 37.3, 35.2, 40.1, 35.1 and 37.7 against the 13.5 threshold. On the clip's own declared ticks the samples are too sparse to sustain the failure, so the scan reads the exemption as STALE there (the worst reads 0, 33.9, 39.8, 35.1 and 37.5 on seeds 0 to 4, all passing). Kept because the dense dumps fail on every seed. Tracked as #1824.
